registered: 2026-11-14, before any execution of this experiment
recording: not recorded by the team runtime; self-recorded manifest. The in-process runtime gates of all programs are satisfied by a local stand-in (fresh directory with 'continue' pre-created) that keeps each runtime.json snapshot but performs no external approval or spec comparison.
protocol_reference: configs/parent-2026-11-12-protocol.json (copied unchanged from the 2026-11-12 context bundle)
question: With all implementations timed on the same GPU in one session, how does the range-split bit-packed scorer's batch-1 latency compare with the adapted GPUSparse monolithic baseline, the CSR full-byte pruner (B16, B32) and the CSR exhaustive control?
hypothesis: All five implementations return identical canonical top-10 lists. The latency ratios are empirical; the 2026-11-13 unpaired observation (0.2047 ms vs published 0.8831 ms monolithic) predicts a ratio below 1 but is not assumed.

csr-full-byte-b16.boundary: host dense weight construction (vocabulary-sized), weight H2D, seed scoring/selection, full-byte bounds, compaction and count D2H, survivor scoring, global selection, winner D2H, event synchronisation

csr-exhaustive-b32.same_as: csr-full-byte-b16 driver, execution mode 0 (no seed, bounds or compaction; every block scored)
csr-exhaustive-b32.choice: B32 chosen for the single exhaustive control because the CSR block scorer launches 32 threads per block; at B16 half of each warp idles. The 2026-11-12 study had no exhaustive control.

differences_between_implementations: Host language: range-bitpack and CSR are C++ drivers; monolithic is Python/Torch with Triton kernels.

Query upload: range-bitpack uploads only the query's (term, weight) pairs; monolithic uploads a padded term/weight pair of length max query terms (95); CSR uploads a dense 28,679-entry weight vector (about 115 KB).

Index layout: range-split bit-packed term-major blocks (2.66 B/posting); monolithic CSC with int32 positions + float32 impacts (8 B/posting); CSR forward lists with uint32 terms + uint8 impacts plus full-byte bound planes for the pruners.
Selection: range-bitpack per-range local top-k plus one-block merge; monolithic packed int64 keys and torch.topk; CSR hierarchical local top-k.

Correctness checks inside the timing processes differ (monolithic compares each output with the reference after timing each query, outside its wall clock); every implementation's saved top-k is compared with the CPU oracle after its process.

correctness_before_timing.range-bitpack: tests/check_range_bitpack.py fixtures; 500 queries with in-driver CPU verification
correctness_before_timing.monolithic: 11 fixtures from tests/prepare_precision_fixture.py plus the parent's above-2^24 'high' fixture, each at k=1/10/128, BLOCK_PL=512 (36 configurations; the parent also ran PL128 and an intentional gate rejection, which are not repeated); 500 real queries with --verify 1
correctness_before_timing.csr: 500 real queries with in-driver CPU verification for B16, B32 and exhaustive B32 (the driver's fixtures passed in its merged parent studies and the source is unchanged)
correctness_before_timing.oracle_comparison: every real-data output file compared with the CPU oracle by experiments/2026-11-13-range-bitpack/analysis/compare_topk.py
correctness_before_timing.rule: any failure stops the run before timing; nothing is retried automatically

timing.process_order_note: rotations by 0, 2 and 4 positions; each implementation occupies a different slot in each round
timing.gpu_check: before each process wait until nvidia-smi lists no compute process (poll every 60 s, abort after 60 min); record GPU state
timing.launch: nohup on cuda5; independent of the laptop connection
timing.during_timing_check: every warm-up and measured top-10 of every process compared with the CPU oracle; monolithic also runs its own post-timing integer validation

analysis.script: analysis/analyze_paired.py (standard library; same estimator as the parent's analysis/analyze.py)
analysis.reduction: per process, median wall latency of each query over the 20 measured rounds
analysis.primary: for each baseline, geometric mean over the 1,500 paired query/process ratios range-bitpack / baseline (process p paired with process p)
analysis.uncertainty: 10,000-draw crossed query/process bootstrap, seed 20261114, linear-interpolated 2.5/97.5% quantiles; conditional on this calibration set and session
analysis.secondary: inverse ratios; CSR B16/B32 over monolithic as a replication check of the 2026-11-12 result (2.8762, 3.5333); CSR B32 pruned over exhaustive; pooled descriptive medians
analysis.decision_rule: range-bitpack is called faster than a baseline in this calibration scope only if the upper end of its interval is below 1, with zero canonical mismatches

not_in_this_registration: held-out queries, k other than 10, batch > 1, range-size sweep, kernel breakdown, other GPUs
